headings: Trademarks, Service Marks and Domain Names
paragraphs: The Company is a value added information technology ("IT") distribution and solutions company. The Company primarily operates through its "Distribution" segment, which distributes emerging and disruptive technologies to corporate resellers, value added resellers ("VARs"), consultants and systems integrators worldwide under the name "Climb Channel Solutions". The Company also operates a smaller segment called "Solutions", which is a cloud solutions provider and value-added reseller of software, hardware and services for customers worldwide under the name "Grey Matter". Across both segments, we offer an extensive line of products from leading software vendors and tools for virtualization/cloud computing, security, networking, storage and infrastructure management, application lifecycle management and other technically sophisticated domains, as well as computer hardware.
The Company was incorporated in Delaware in 1982. Our common stock, par value $0.01 per share ("Common Stock"), is listed on The NASDAQ Global Market under the symbol "CLMB".

In our Distribution segment, which accounted for approximately 96% of our consolidated net sales and 87% of our consolidated gross profit during the year ended December 31, 2025, we distribute technology products from software developers, software vendors or original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") to resellers, and system integrators worldwide. We purchase software, maintenance/service agreements, networking/storage/security equipment and complementary products from our vendors and sell them to our reseller customers. The large majority of hardware products we sell are "drop shipped" directly to the customers, which reduces physical handling by the Company and required investment in inventory. Generally, a vendor authorizes a limited number of companies to act as distributors of their product and sell their product to resellers. Our reseller customers include VARs, corporate resellers, government resellers, system integrators, direct marketers, and national IT superstores. We combine our core strengths in customer service, marketing, distribution, credit and billing to allow our customers to achieve greater efficiencies in time to market in the IT channel in a cost-effective manner.

While our Distribution business is characterized by low gross profit as a percentage of gross billings, or gross billings margin, and price competition, we have been able to operate profitably by leveraging an efficient and scalable business model with low capital investment requirements. The large majority of the products we sell are either digital products such as license authorizations, third party maintenance contracts, or hardware that is drop-shipped to the end customer directly by the vendor. We utilize electronic data interchange ("EDI") and other automation tools to fulfill these orders on a cost-efficient basis. We also maintain relatively low inventory balances relative to our gross billings and enjoy what we believe is favorable credit from our vendor partners, allowing us to deploy a capital efficient model as reflected by our return on equity and pre-tax income as a percentage of gross profit generated.

In our Distribution segment, we are highly dependent on the end-market demand for the products we sell, and on our partners' strategic initiatives and business models. This end-market demand is influenced by many factors including the introduction of new products, replacement and renewal cycles for existing products, competitive products, overall economic growth and general business activity. A difficult and challenging economic environment may also lead to consolidation or decline in the industry and increased price-based competition. We continually review the marketplace to identify new, emerging and disruptive vendors and products to potentially add to our vendor partners.
The Company operates distribution facilities in Millersville, Maryland and Dublin, Ireland.

We also provide comprehensive IT solutions directly to end users through our Solutions segment, which accounted for approximately 4% of our consolidated net sales and 13% of our consolidated gross profit during the year ended December 31, 2025. Products in this segment are acquired directly from OEMs, software developers or distributors and sold to end users. We provide customer service, billing, sales and marketing support in this segment and provide extended payment terms to facilitate sales.

We view acquisitions as an important part of our strategic growth plan. In 2020, we completed two acquisitions to add scale, broaden our geographic footprint, expand partner relationships and add cloud support capabilities. In 2022, we completed an acquisition that expanded our sales presence in the United Kingdom software distribution markets.

In 2023, we completed the acquisition of Data Solutions Holdings Limited ("Data Solutions"), which further expanded our geographic footprint and partner relationships in the United Kingdom and Ireland software distribution markets. In 2024, we completed the acquisition of Douglas Stewart Software & Services, LLC ("DSS"), which further strengthened our reach in the North American K-12 and higher education software distribution markets.
We plan to continue to evaluate acquisition opportunities as part of our overall capital allocation strategy and continuing growth plan.

An essential part of our ongoing operations and strategic growth plan in our Distribution segment is the continued recruitment of software vendors for which we become authorized distributors of their products. Through our Distribution segment, we sell a wide variety of technology products from a broad range of software vendors and manufacturers, such as Adobe, Bluebeam Software, Dark Trace, Delinea, ExtraHop, Fortinet, Micro Focus, Microsoft, SmartBear Software, SolarWinds, Sophos, TechSmith and Trend Micro. On a continuous basis, we screen new vendors and products for inclusion in our line card based on their features, quality, price, profit margins and current market trends. Developing a diverse vendor base is a key element of our business strategy. We focus on establishing deep relationships with our vendor and reseller partners by providing specialized product training to our sales force and the use of dedicated sales teams. We have also established an efficient ordering process with our key partners through the implementation of electronic ordering and other processes adapted to their requirements. As a result, our relationships with our key vendor partners tend to be long-term in nature despite the absence of long-term contracts, with a significant portion of sales derived from annually recurring renewals of software maintenance and subscription agreements related to our partners embedded base of customers utilizing their software products. Additionally, a key part of our strategic growth plan is to provide a high level of support to select emerging and disruptive technology vendors through our Climb Elevate program to develop future relationships throughout the growth cycle of a vendor partner. The Climb Elevate program allows resellers and vendors to connect through the Company for products typically outside of the main line-card.

In our Solutions business, an essential part of our strategic growth plan is to pursue opportunities with higher growth prospects and gross margin characteristics through the sale of specialty products, services and cloud offerings. Through acquisitions in the prior years, we added certain technical and administrative support capabilities to enable us to resell cloud and software as a service products ("SaaS") including Microsoft products in the United Kingdom. Our strategic growth plan is to expand our cloud offerings by leveraging these support services to other markets and products.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company had no major vendors that accounted for greater than 10% of our consolidated purchases during the year, compared to one vendor that accounted for 10% and 14% of our consolidated purchases, respectively, for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023. For the year ended December 31, 2025, our largest five vendors generated approximately 29% of our consolidated purchases. The loss of a key vendor or group of vendors could disrupt our product availability and otherwise have an adverse effect on the Company.

The Company predominantly sells third party software, software subscriptions, and maintenance. Sales of hardware and peripherals consistently represented 8% in 2025 and 6% of our gross billings, an operational metric, in 2024 and 2023.

headings: Risks Related to our Business and Industry
paragraphs: Investors should carefully consider the risk factors set forth below as well as the other information contained in this Annual Report. Any of the following risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations and could cause our results to differ from the "forward-looking statements" contained in this Annual Report. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or those currently viewed by us to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.

We serve customers and have locations throughout the world and are subject to terrorist attacks, acts of war, natural disasters, global pandemic and other similar risks, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Worldwide economic conditions remain uncertain due to the persistence of inflation, elevated interest rates, market volatility and adverse effects on product demand connected to geopolitical developments including tariff uncertainty, and other disruptions to global and regional economies and markets. Terrorist attacks, acts of war, natural disasters, global pandemics or other disasters or public health concerns in regions of the world where we have operations could result in the disruption of our business. Such acts have created, and continue to create, economic and political uncertainties and have contributed to global economic instability. Specifically, these acts, pandemics, disasters and health concerns can result in increased travel restrictions and extended shutdowns of certain businesses in the region, as well as social, economic, or labor instability. Disruptions in affected regions over a prolonged period could have a material adverse impact on our business and our financial results.

Changes in the information technology industry and/or economic environment may reduce demand for the products and services we sell. Our results of operations are influenced by a variety of factors, including the condition of the IT industry, general economic conditions, seasonal buying by end-users, shifts in demand for, or availability of, computer products and software and IT services and industry introductions of new products, upgrades or methods of distribution. We typically sell to our customers on a purchase order basis, rather than pursuant to long-term contracts or contracts with minimum purchase requirements. Consequently, our sales are subject to demand variability by our customers. The information technology products industry is characterized by abrupt changes in technology, rapid changes in customer preferences, short product life cycles and evolving industry standards. Net sales can be dependent on demand for specific product categories, and any change in demand for or supply of such products could have a material adverse effect on our net sales, and/or cause us to record write-downs of obsolete inventory, if we fail to react in a timely manner to such changes.

We rely on our vendor partners for product availability, marketing funds, purchasing incentives and competitive products to sell. If we are unable to maintain our relationships with our vendor partners, if the vendor partners materially change the terms of their existing agreements with us or we fail to abide by the terms of such agreements, if our vendor partners cease selling their products through distribution generally, or if supply chain shortages and other disruptions occur, our business could be materially adversely affected. We acquire products for resale both directly from manufacturers and indirectly from distributors. A substantial portion of the products we acquire are purchased from vendor partners with which we have entered into non-exclusive distribution agreements. These agreements are typically cancellable at any time or on short notice (generally 30 days). The loss of a vendor partner could cause a disruption in the availability of products. Additionally, there is no assurance that as manufacturers continue to or increasingly sell directly to end users and through the distribution channel, that they will not limit or curtail the availability of their products to distributors/resellers like us. To the extent that our vendor partners reduce the number of products they sell through the distribution channel or cease selling their products through the distribution channel entirely, experience disruptions in their supply chains, cease to continue doing business with us, or are unable to continue to meet or significantly alter their obligations, our business could be materially adversely affected. Our inability to obtain a sufficient quantity of products, or an allocation of products from a manufacturer in a way that favors one of our competitors, or competing distribution channels, relative to us, could cause us to be unable to fill clients' orders in a timely manner, or at all, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition. In addition, to the extent our vendor partners modify the terms of their contracts to the detriment of us, limit supplies due to capacity constraints or other factors, or cancel such contracts or exercise remedies thereunder due to our breach of contract terms, there could be a material adverse effect on our business. We also rely on our vendor partners to provide funds for us to market their products, including through our online marketing efforts, and to provide purchasing incentives to us. If any of the vendor partners that have historically provided these benefits to us decides to reduce such benefits, our expenses would increase, adversely affecting our results of operations.

The IT products and services industry is intensely competitive and actions of competitors, including manufacturers of products we sell, can negatively affect our business. Competition has been based primarily on price, product availability, speed of delivery, credit availability and quality and breadth of product lines and, increasingly, also is based on the ability to tailor specific solutions to client needs. We compete with manufacturers, including manufacturers of products we sell, as well as a large number and wide variety of marketers and resellers of IT products and services. In addition, manufacturers are increasing the volume of software products they distribute electronically directly to end-users and in the future, will likely pay lower referral fees for sales of certain software licensing agreements sold by us. Further, the manufacturer landscape has continued to experience consolidation, which could negatively impact us if the surviving, consolidated manufacturers decide to exclude us from their supply chains, and which could expose us to increased pricing and dependence on a smaller number of suppliers, among other risks. Increasing consolidation in the industries where our manufacturers operate may occur as companies combine to achieve further economies of scale and other synergies, which could result in reduced supplies, as companies seek to eliminate duplicative product lines and services, and increased prices, which could have a material adverse effect on our business. Generally, pricing is very aggressive in the industry, and we expect pricing pressures to continue. We compete for both customers and manufacturers in a highly competitive international environment against other large multinational and national distributors and resellers, as well as numerous other smaller, specialized competitors who generally focus on narrower market sectors, products, or industries. Such robust competition broadly, and within each market sector and geography, creates pricing and margin pressure and continuous demand for us to improve service and product offerings There can be no assurance that we will be able to negotiate prices as favorable as those negotiated by our competitors or that we will be able to offset the effects of price reductions with an increase in the number of clients, higher net sales, cost reductions, or greater sales of services, which service sales typically are delivered at higher gross margins, or otherwise. Price reductions by our competitors that we either cannot or choose not to match, could result in an erosion of our market share and/or reduced sales or, to the extent we match, such reductions, could result in reduced operating margins, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

If we fail to adequately invest successfully in and introduce digital, artificial intelligence ("AI"), and other technological developments, or our suppliers are not able to continue to offer competitive components and electronic computing solutions, it could materially adversely impact results. Our industry is subject to rapid and significant technological changes, and our ability to meet our customers' needs and expectations is key to our ability to grow sales and earnings. Our customers and suppliers increasingly expect our platforms to include digital technologies to facilitate distribution of components and electronic computing solutions over time. For example, the ability of customers to access their accounts, place orders, and otherwise interface with us using digital technology is an important aspect of the distribution industry, and distribution companies are rapidly introducing new digital and other technology-driven products and services that aim to offer a better customer experience and reduce costs. If we are unable to maintain and enhance our digital platforms, cloud platforms, and AI-related tools to keep pace with competitors and align with evolving customer and supplier expectations and demands, it could adversely impact our sales revenues and ability to retain existing, and attract new, customers.

headings: 商標、服務標誌及網域名稱
paragraphs: 本公司為一家附加價值的資訊科技（"IT"）通路與解決方案公司。本公司主要透過其 "Distribution" 應報告分部運作，該分部以 "Climb Channel Solutions" 名義，向全球企業通路商、附加價值通路商（"VARs"）、顧問及系統整合商，分銷新興且具有顛覆性的科技產品。本公司亦運作一個規模較小的應報告分部，稱為 "Solutions"，該分部為全球客戶提供雲端解決方案及軟體、硬體與服務的附加價值通路商，名稱為 "Grey Matter"。在兩個應報告分部中，我們提供來自知名軟體供應商的廣泛產品線，以及用於虛擬化/雲端計算、安全性、網路、儲存與基礎設施管理、應用程式生命週期管理及其他技術複雜領域的工具，以及電腦硬體。
本公司於1982年在特拉華州註冊成立。本公司發行的普通股，每股面值0.01美元（"Common Stock"），於NASDAQ全球市場上市交易，股票代碼為 "CLMB"。

在Distribution應報告分部，該分部在2025年12月31日財年中，約佔本公司合併淨銷售額的96%及合併毛利率的87%，我們分銷來自軟體開發商、軟體供應商或原始設備製造商（"OEMs"）的科技產品，至全球的通路商與系統整合商。我們從供應商處購入軟體、維護/服務合約、網路/儲存/安全性設備及補充性產品，並銷售給通路商客戶。我們銷售的大多數硬體產品均為"直送"至客戶手中，這可減少本公司之實體處理作業，並降低存貨所需之投資。通常，供應商會授權有限數量的公司作為其產品的分銷商，並銷售其產品至通路商。我們的通路商客戶包括VARs、企業通路商、政府通路商、系統整合商、直接行銷商及國家IT超級商店。我們結合在客戶服務、行銷、分銷、信用與帳單處理方面的核心優勢，使客戶能以更具成本效益的方式，在IT通路中提升產品上市時間的效率。

雖然我們的Distribution業務以銷售產品的總體銷售金額的毛利率（即總體銷售金額毛利率）為低，且價格競爭激烈，但我們已能透過運用高效且可擴展的業務模式，以及低資本投資需求，維持獲利。我們銷售的大多數產品為數位產品，例如授權許可、第三方維護合約，或由供應商直接送達最終客戶的硬體。我們利用電子資料交換（"EDI"）及其他自動化工具，以低成本效益的方式處理這些訂單。我們也維持相對於總體銷售金額而言較低的存貨水準，並享有我們認為有利的信用條件，使我們能運用資本效率高的模式，反映在我們的權益回報率及稅前收入佔總體銷售金額毛利率的比例上。
在Distribution應報告分部，我們高度依賴所銷售產品的最終市場需求，以及合作夥伴的戰略計畫與業務模式。此最終市場需求受許多因素影響，包括新產品的推出、現有產品的更換與續約週期、競爭產品、總體經濟成長與整體商業活動。困難且具有挑戰性的經濟環境也可能導致產業整併或衰退，並增加基於價格的競爭。我們持續審視市場，以識別可能加入合作夥伴的全新、興起且具有顛覆性的供應商與產品。
本公司在馬裏蘭州米勒斯維爾及愛爾蘭都柏林設有通路設施。
我們也透過Solutions應報告分部，直接向終端用戶提供完整的IT解決方案，該分部在2025年12月31日財年中，約佔本公司合併淨銷售額的4%及合併毛利率的13%。此分部的產品直接從OEMs、軟體開發商或通路商處取得，並銷售給終端用戶。我們在該分部提供客戶服務、帳單處理、銷售與行銷支援，並提供延長付款條件以促進銷售。
我們認為收購是我們戰略成長計畫的重要組成部分。2020年，我們完成兩項收購，以增加規模、擴大地理足跡、拓展合作夥伴關係並增加雲端支援能力。2022年，我們完成一項收購，以擴大在英國軟體通路市場的銷售據點。

2023 年，本公司完成對 Data Solutions Holdings Limited（"Data Solutions"）的收購，進一步擴大了本公司在英國與愛爾蘭軟體分銷市場的地理足跡與合作夥伴關係。2024 年，本公司完成對 Douglas Stewart Software & Services, LLC（"DSS"）的收購，進一步強化了本公司在北美 K-12 及高等教育軟體分銷市場的影響力。
本公司計畫持續評估收購機會，作為本公司整體資金配置策略與持續成長計畫的一部分。

在本公司分銷分部的持續運作與戰略成長計畫中，持續招募軟體供應商並成為其產品的授權分銷商是其中一個重要部分。透過本公司分銷分部，本公司銷售來自廣泛軟體供應商與製造商的多樣化科技產品，例如 Adobe、Bluebeam Software、Dark Trace、Delinea、ExtraHop、Fortinet、Micro Focus、Microsoft、SmartBear Software、SolarWinds、Sophos、TechSmith 以及 Trend Micro。本公司持續評估新供應商與產品，以根據其功能、品質、價格、利潤率與當前市場趨勢，決定是否納入本公司產品線。建立多元化的供應商基礎是本公司業務策略的關鍵要素。本公司致力於與供應商與經銷商夥伴建立深入的關係，透過為銷售團隊提供專門的產品培訓，以及設立專屬銷售團隊來實現。本公司亦透過實施電子訂購及其他適應其需求的流程，與關鍵合作夥伴建立高效的訂購流程。因此，儘管缺乏長期契約，本公司與關鍵供應商夥伴的關係往往具有長期性，並有相當大比例的銷售來自於軟體維護與訂閱協議的年度續約，這些協議與本公司合作夥伴的客戶基礎有關。此外，本公司戰略成長計畫的關鍵部分是透過 Climb Elevate 程式為選擇性的新興與顛覆性科技供應商提供高水平的支援，以在供應商夥伴的成長週期中建立未來的關係。Climb Elevate 程式允許經銷商與供應商透過本公司連接，以銷售通常不在主要產品線中的產品。
在本公司解決方案業務中，戰略成長計畫的重要部分是透過銷售專業產品、服務與雲端方案，追求具有更高成長潛力與毛利率特徵的機會。透過過去幾年的收購，本公司已增加某些技術與行政支援能力，以使本公司能夠銷售雲端與軟體即服務產品（"SaaS"），包括英國市場的 Microsoft 產品。本公司戰略成長計畫是透過這些支援服務，擴展雲端方案至其他市場與產品。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司在當年未有任何單一供應商佔據本公司合併採購總額的 10% 以上，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日分別有單一供應商佔據 10% 與 14% 的合併採購總額相比。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司前五大供應商產生約 29% 的合併採購總額。失去關鍵供應商或一羣供應商可能會干擾本公司產品的供應，並對本公司造成不利影響。
本公司主要銷售第三方軟體、軟體訂閱與維護服務。硬體與週邊設備的銷售在 2025 年佔比為 8%，在 2024 年與 2023 年的營業收入（營運指標）中分別佔比為 6%。

paragraphs: 投資人應謹慎考量下列所列之風險因素，以及本年度財務報告中所包含之其他資訊。任何下列風險均可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響，並可能導致本公司結果與本年度財務報告中所載之「前瞻性陳述」有所差異。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，亦可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。

本公司服務客戶，並在全球各地設有營運據點，因此面臨恐怖攻擊、戰爭行為、自然災害、全球性疫情及其他類似風險，這些風險可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。全球經濟情況仍不確定，這是因為通貨膨脹持續存在、利率偏高、市場波動以及與地緣政治發展相關的產品需求受到負面影響，包括關稅不確定性，以及其他對全球及區域經濟與市場的幹擾。在本公司營運地區發生恐怖攻擊、戰爭行為、自然災害、全球性疫情或其他災難或公共衛生問題，可能導致本公司業務中斷。這些行為已造成，並持續造成經濟與政治的不確定性，並已對全球經濟穩定性產生影響。具體而言，這些行為、疫情、災難及健康問題可能導致該地區旅行限制增加，以及某些企業的營運中斷時間延長，同時也造成社會、經濟或勞動市場的不穩定。受影響地區若長時間出現中斷，可能對本公司業務及財務結果造成重大且不利的影響。

資訊科技產業及/或經濟環境的變化可能降低本公司所銷售產品與服務的需求。本公司營運成果受多種因素影響，包括資訊科技產業的狀況、總體經濟情況、終端用戶的季節性採購、電腦產品與軟體及資訊科技服務的需求變化或供應情況，以及產業內新產品、升級版或分銷方式的引入。本公司通常以訂單方式銷售給客戶，而非根據長期契約或最低採購量契約。因此，本公司銷售受客戶需求變動的影響。資訊科技產品產業特徵為技術變更迅速、客戶偏好快速改變、產品生命週期短且產業標準不斷演進。淨銷售額可能依賴特定產品類別的需求，任何該類產品的需求或供應變化，均可能對本公司淨銷售額造成重大且不利的影響，或導致本公司因未能及時應對這些變化而需記提過時存貨減損。

本公司依賴供應商夥伴提供產品供應、行銷經費、採購激勵措施及可銷售的競爭性產品。若本公司無法維持與供應商夥伴的關係，若供應商夥伴大幅變更與本公司現有契約的條款，或本公司未能遵守這些契約條款，若供應商夥伴停止透過一般分銷渠道銷售其產品，或若供應鏈短缺及其他幹擾發生，本公司業務可能受到重大且不利的影響。本公司透過直接向製造商及間接透過經銷商取得產品以進行轉售。本公司取得的產品中，有相當大一部分是透過與本公司簽訂非獨佔分銷契約的供應商夥伴所購買。這些契約通常可隨時終止，或在短時間內（通常為30天）終止。失去某供應商夥伴可能導致產品供應中斷。此外，目前尚無保證，製造商持續或更積極地直接向終端用戶銷售產品，並透過分銷渠道銷售，他們不會限制或減少對經銷商/轉售商如本公司所提供的產品供應。若供應商夥伴減少透過分銷渠道銷售產品的數量，或完全停止透過分銷渠道銷售產品，經驗到供應鏈中斷，停止與本公司繼續業務往來，或無法繼續履行或大幅改變其義務，本公司業務可能受到重大且不利的影響。本公司若無法取得足夠的產品，或製造商在分配產品時偏袒競爭對手或競爭性分銷渠道，相對於本公司，可能導致本公司無法及時或完全履行客戶訂單，這可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。此外，若供應商夥伴修改其契約條款對本公司不利，因容量限制或其他因素而限制供應，或因本公司違反契約條款而終止契約或行使契約條款下的救濟措施，可能對本公司業務造成重大且不利的影響。本公司亦依賴供應商夥伴提供經費，以協助本公司行銷其產品，包括透過線上行銷活動，並提供給本公司採購激勵措施。若任何曾提供這些好處的供應商夥伴決定減少這些好處，本公司費用將增加，對營運成果造成不利影響。

資訊科技產品與服務產業競爭激烈，競爭對手的行動，包括我們所銷售產品的製造商，可能對本公司業務造成負面影響。競爭主要基於價格、產品供應、交貨速度、信貸可得性及產品線的品質與廣度，且 increasingly 也基於能為客戶需求提供特定解決方案的能力。我們與製造商、包括我們所銷售產品的製造商，以及大量且種類繁多的資訊科技產品與服務行銷商與轉售商競爭。此外，製造商正在增加透過電子方式直接向終端用戶分銷軟體產品的數量，並在未來，很可能會為我們銷售的軟體授權契約支付較低的介紹費用。此外，製造商產業持續經歷合併，若存活下來的合併後製造商決定排除我們於其供應鏈中，這可能對我們造成負面影響，並可能使我們面臨更高的價格與對較少供應商的依賴，以及其他風險。資訊科技產業中製造商所處產業的合併情況可能持續發生，因為公司結合以實現進一步的規模經濟與其他協同效益，這可能導致供應減少，因為公司試圖消除重複的產品線與服務，並導致價格上漲，這可能對本公司業務造成重大且不利的影響。通常而言，產業中的價格競爭非常激烈，我們預期價格壓力將持續。我們在高度競爭的國際環境中，與其他大型跨國與國家分銷商與轉售商競爭，以及眾多其他較小且專業化的競爭對手，這些競爭對手通常專注於較窄的市場部門、產品或產業。這種強烈的競爭，以及在每個市場部門與地理區域內的競爭，造成價格與邊際利益壓力，並持續要求我們改善服務與產品的提供。無法保證我們將能與競爭對手 negotiated 一樣有利的價格，或我們將能透過增加客戶數量、提高淨銷售額、成本降低或服務銷售增加（服務銷售通常以較高的毛利率進行）來抵消價格下降的影響，或以其他方式。若競爭對手的價格下降，而我們無法或選擇不跟進，這可能導致我們的市場佔有率下降或銷售減少，若我們跟進，則可能導致營運邊際利益下降，任何情況均可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。

若本公司未能成功投資並推出數位、人工智慧（"AI"）及其他科技發展，或供應商無法持續提供具競爭力的零組件與電子計算解決方案，可能對結果造成重大且不利的影響。本公司所屬產業面臨快速且重大的科技變革，本公司能否滿足客戶的需求與期望，是本公司能否增加銷售與獲利的關鍵。客戶與供應商日益期待本公司平台包含數位科技，以協助未來零組件與電子計算解決方案的分銷。例如，客戶透過數位科技存取帳戶、下訂單，並以其他方式與本公司互動的能力，是分銷產業的重要方面，而分銷公司正迅速引入新的數位及其他科技驅動的產品與服務，以提供更好的客戶體驗並降低成本。若本公司無法維持並提升數位平台、雲端平台及與人工智慧相關的工具，以跟上競爭對手並符合客戶與供應商不斷演變的期待與需求，可能對本公司銷售收入與保留現有客戶及吸引新客戶的能力造成不利影響。
